transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Rana (Veridian Head of Platform), Elena Morales (Veridian CTO), Liam O'Connor (Veridian SRE)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, discuss expansion to additional EU region, bump in reserved capacity (Dedicated), timeline for contract extension, security docs and pilot scope. Agreed to send updated pricing and SOC2 artifacts; follow-up pilot week of 2026-04-20.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity sizing, additional regions (EU), private vs dedicated tradeoffs, SSO/KMS/audit logs, pilot scope and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time, we'll keep this crisp, quick renewal and expansion check-in for veridian. maya and i are here from redwood.
[00:08] Samir Rana: thanks jordan, yeah we got the renewal notice last week, elena's on for the capacity discussion, liam's gonna cover infra constraints.
[00:15] Elena Morales: hi all, yup, moving fast on our end — main asks: add eu region, about 2x current capacity for Q3, and want to extend the contract for 12 months. want to understand pricing and timing.
[00:28] Maya Chen: great, thanks elena. quick recap: currently on Redwood Hosted with a small dedicated commit for peak jobs, correct? you have some dedicated slots for our batch rerank workloads but most realtime goes through hosted. is that still accurate?
[00:40] Samir Rana: yes that's right. realtime frontends go to hosted, some critical pathways are pinned to dedicated. overall monthly tokens have gone up ~1.7x since jan.
[00:50] Jordan Patel: perfect. so the ask is: 1) renewal + 12 months, 2) increase Dedicated capacity to handle ~2x peak q3, 3) add eu-west region for lower latency and data residency.
[01:03] Liam O'Connor: and we need private VPC peering for some datasets — can you confirm options for Private deployment vs Dedicated in a VPC? last time the doc had a few names swapped — Redwood Private vs Redwood Dedicated, little fuzzy in notes.
[01:18] Maya Chen: sure — high level: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our region, still managed by Redwood control plane (good for throughput predictability). Private is the VPC/on-prem option where you control networking and keys. for most customers adding eu region we do a Dedicated pool in eu-west, and if you need on-prem or fully isolated control plane, that's Private. i'll share the chart after.
[01:32] Jordan Patel: note on cost tradeoffs: Dedicated increases monthly commit but much lower per-token unit cost; Private adds platform fee and extra ops, so we usually see higher TCO but better isolation.
[01:41] [03:15] Elena Morales: what's the latency delta if we add eu region for our european customers? we saw 120-150ms p95 from northeast region now.
[03:25] Maya Chen: if we place inference in eu-west you should see p95 drop to ~30-50ms for eu clients — depending on seq length and model. caveat: small variance if you use larger context lengths or certain quantized model variants.
[03:40] Samir Rana: for capacity sizing — what does 2x mean in your terms? do you mean GPU equivalents or token RPS?
[03:46] Jordan Patel: good question; we'd prefer token RPS target. can you give us current token RPS and desired?
[03:52] Samir Rana: current token RPS at peak is 14k tokens/sec across all endpoints, aiming for 28k tokens/sec to be safe.
[04:02] Maya Chen: ok that's helpful. rough mapping: depending on model family, 28k tokens/sec maps to approx 6-8 gpus of the current fleet (varies by model and quantization). i'll include a sizing table in the follow-up.
[04:15] [06:00] Liam O'Connor: security items: we need SOC2, ISO certs, audit log retention limits, and we use an internal KMS. can the private option bring our own key (BYOK) or integrate with our HSM?
[06:12] Maya Chen: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and BYOK patterns; Dedicated (hosted) supports customer-managed keys via KMS in some configurations — i'll clarify what's available in eu region. SOC2 and ISO docs are available — i'll attach them.
[06:28] Elena Morales: also SSO and RBAC — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[06:34] Jordan Patel: we support SSO SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC on console, and audit logs can be routed to your SIEM. maya will confirm retention windows and export options.
[06:45] [09:10] Samir Rana: pricing — ballpark increment for doubling Dedicated and adding eu region? we want to understand both committed and burst costs.
[09:19] Jordan Patel: high level: doubling committed Dedicated capacity is roughly a 1.9x on committed spend (volume discounts at scale) and region adds a fixed monthly region premium. i'll send a revised quote with line items: committed capacity, region standby reservoir, burst tokens, and Private platform fee if you choose that.
[09:34] Maya Chen: and note there are operational knobs: batching, kv/prefix caching and quantization profiles that can lower the effective GPU need. we can run a perf test to estimate exact hours.
[09:45] [12:00] Liam O'Connor: on the perf side, can you run a benchmark using our sample prompts? we'd like realistic numbers before signing.
[12:08] Maya Chen: yes — pilot/perf run is typical. we do a 1-2 day benchmark with your prompt set against the candidate model and config. we'll need a sample dataset and expected SLA.
[12:20] Samir Rana: timeline: target to go live with increased capacity by mid-July. contract to be extended starting May 1st so provisioning's aligned. is that feasible?
[12:30] Jordan Patel: timeline is feasible; key path is getting confirmation on token RPS, signing updated MSA/PO, and SOC2 review. provisioning Dedicated pool in eu usually takes 2-3 weeks from PO/commit. Private takes longer (ops scheduling).
[12:45] [16:00] Elena Morales: any blockers on data residency? encrypted at rest is a must and we need contract language about residency for eu customer data.
[16:09] Maya Chen: we support data residency in eu pools; encryption at rest and transit standard. i'll flag legal to provide residency language and the data processing addendum.
[16:20] Samir Rana: competitors — we've been evaluating Anthropic for chat and using Lambda for some in-house spikes. cost and latency are the deciding factors.
[16:29] Jordan Patel: understood, we can show unit economics and also run a TCO comparison for Dedicated vs Anthropic + infra.
[16:35] [21:00] Maya Chen: quick note on model variants — we can provision smaller quantized variants for high-throughput endpoints and larger fp16 for quality-critical endpoints; routing policies can fallback to cheaper models if Dedicated is saturated.
[21:12] Liam O'Connor: does fallback preserve session state? we use long chats.
[21:18] Maya Chen: yes we support kv cache management and session pinning to keep quality; we'll document the limits. there are edge cases with transformer kv eviction at high concurrency that we'll cover.
[21:30] [28:00] Jordan Patel: ok recapping: 1) veridian will extend contract 12 months starting May 1, pending updated quote and SOC2/legal review; 2) veridian requests approx 2x capacity target (28k token RPS) and new eu-west Dedicated pool; 3) pilot/perf run to validate sizing and latency; 4) next steps include updated pricing, SOC2 docs, runbook and VPC requirements.
[28:45] Elena Morales: sounds good. we'll aim to confirm numbers by 2026-04-14.
[28:52] Samir Rana: liam will follow up on firewall and networking items.
[29:00] [34:00] Jordan Patel: i'll send the quote and schedule the perf run once we get Samir's prompt set and liam's network constraints. maya will share security artifacts.
[34:12] Maya Chen: i'll include Console screenshots of latency/cost breakdown and suggested batching/quant profiles.
[34:20] [42:00] Samir Rana: thanks — one more ask: can you include a migration checklist for routing traffic to the new eu region and a rollback plan?
[42:10] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a migration runbook and rollback steps; we'll also suggest canary percentages and monitoring thresholds.
[42:22] Jordan Patel: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[42:28] Elena Morales: thanks, appreciate it.
[42:30] [47:50] End of call.
